title: Top K Frequent Elements
summary: Solve Top K Frequent Elements using the standard optimized interview approach.
hint: Look for the Heap / Priority Queue structure that reduces repeated work.

idea: Count how often each value appears.
Read buckets from high frequency down.

approach: Identify the state or invariant needed for Top K Frequent Elements.
Use Heap / Priority Queue and Hash Map to process the input efficiently.
Update the result while preserving the invariant.
Return the final value after all relevant input is processed.
pseudocode: for frequency from high to low:

desktop: function topKFrequent(nums, k) { const counts = new Map(); for (const n of nums) counts.set(n, (counts.get(n) || 0) + 1); return [...counts.entries()].sort((a,b)=>b[1]-a[1]).slice(0,k).map(x=>x[0]); }

class Solution { public int[] topKFrequent(int[] nums, int k) { Map<Integer,Integer> count = new HashMap<>(); for (int n : nums) count.put(n, count.getOrDefault(n,0)+1); PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a,b) -> count.get(a) - count.get(b)); for (int n : count.keySet()) { pq.add(n); if (pq.size() > k) pq.remove(); } int[] ans = new int[k]; for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--) ans[i] = pq.remove(); return ans; } }
